claim: Patient histories become lifelong digital records
originalWording: Patient histories become lifelong digital records

sources.title: Spiritual Machines: The Merging of Man and Machine — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: P02 Health care in 2009, lifetime-records bullet

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Longitudinal patient histories are ordinarily kept digitally; “lifetime” means accumulating records over a patient’s life, not retroactive digitization of every scrap.
reference.rationale: EHR adoption was still low in the 2008–2009 US baseline, so ordinary digital longitudinal records were only partly realized. By 2014 most US hospitals and more than half of physicians had adopted EHRs; subsequent adoption increased. This supports late longitudinal-database fulfillment.

evidence.title: ONC: National trends in hospital and physician EHR adoption
evidence.note: US series: 2008 hospitals 9%, physicians 17%; 2014 76% and 51%; 2022 99% and 84%. Definitions evolve; adoption does not prove complete interoperable lifetime records..
